title: Customer evidence onboarding: SIEM ingest & RBAC v2 one-pager (draft)
content:
Purpose:
This one-pager is a customer-facing draft that explains how Redwood exposes audit evidence and SIEM-compatible exports during onboarding. Focused on customers who need RBAC v2 evidence, live audit streams, and automated evidence packaging for third-party assessments.

Scope:
- What customers receive: streaming audit logs (Kafka/HTTPS), periodic evidence bundles (S3 export), RBAC v2 role/permission snapshots, and curated mapping for common SIEMs (Splunk, Sumo Logic, QRadar).
- What this doc is not: internal infra runbooks or deep schema evolution notes.

High-level flow (customer view):
1) Kickoff: security onboarding call, alignment on required evidence, compliance deadline, and contact points.
2) Atlas mapping: we map your control queries to Redwood audit events and RBAC constructs.
3) Access & transport: choose export method (forwarder, secure S3 share, or push API). Establish TLS + mTLS, IP allowlist, and KMS key for encrypted bundles.
4) Validation: test events, sampling window, and retention checks.
5) Handover: create evidence package + runbook for customer auditors and their SIEM ingestion team.

What we provide (deliverables):
- Real-time event stream (optional): JSON event per action with ISO8601 timestamp, request_id, actor, resource, action, outcome, and metadata.
- Periodic audit bundle: zipped CSV/NDJSON of events for requested time ranges, plus RBAC snapshot JSON and policy hashes.
- Evidence manifest: list of files, retention window, KMS key id, and hashes for integrity check.
- SIEM mapping guide: example field mapping + recommended ingest settings.

Sample minimal audit event (customer-facing example):
- timestamp: 2026-03-01T15:22:03Z
- request_id: rq_01F8Y2K3JX1P0
- actor: user:alice@example.com
- actor_id: usr_7a8b9c
- role: data-analyst (from RBAC v2 snapshot)
- resource_type: model.endpoint
- resource_id: ep_prod_1
- action: generate.text
- params: {"prompt_len": 48, "max_tokens": 256}
- outcome: success
- latency_ms: 92
- node_id: gpu-serve-12
- tenant_id: acct_9842
- trace_id: tr_33a7
- extra: {"kv_cache_hit": true}

RBAC v2 snapshot (what we export):
- roles.json: list of role objects (role_id, name, description, policy_version, created_at)
- bindings.json: user/group/sa -> role bindings (subject_type, subject_id, role_id, scope)
- policies.json: granular allow/deny statements with resource selectors and action lists
- policy_hashes.txt: deterministic hash per policy bundle for auditor verification

SIEM field mapping (recommended):
- event_time -> timestamp
- src_actor -> actor_id
- actor_email -> actor
- user_role -> role
- resource -> resource_type:resource_id (concatenate)
- action -> action
- result -> outcome
- agent -> node_id
- meta.trace -> trace_id
- meta.latency_ms -> latency_ms

Typical onboarding timeline (rough):
- Week 0: NDA + scoping call
- Week 1: Access provisioning (customer to confirm forwarder/S3/KMS) + schema selection
- Week 2: Test export + validation, small sampling window
- Week 3: Full export run + evidence bundle delivery; start retention verification
- Week 4: Handover documentation + optional canary SIEM ingest

Customer responsibilities (minimal):
- Provide contact for SIEM ingestion and network admins for allowlists
- Decide export method and schedule key rotation windows
- Confirm retention policy and regulatory constraints (e.g., 7y for financial audits)

Redwood responsibilities (during onboarding):
- Produce event streams and evidence bundles as agreed
- Map RBAC v2 constructs to exported role objects and provide a readable policy summary
- Provide integrity checks (hashes) and signature metadata for bundles
- Offer sample parsers for Splunk and Sumo Logic (Python/NDJSON examples)

Open questions / negotiation points (for onboarding call):
- Do you require per-token content retention in audit logs? (we typically redact model I/O by default; can provide hashed artifacts)
- Preferred transport: push vs pull? Customers behind strict firewalls often prefer S3 + VPC endpoint.
- Minimum retention window vs cost: where to strike balance for compliance vs unit economics.

Compliance and attestation notes:
- Evidence bundles include timestamps and cryptographic hashes; we can provide signed manifests on request (additional SLA).
- RBAC v2 snapshots are exported with policy_version metadata to help auditors reconcile historical changes.
- For FedRAMP / HIPAA customers we'll include additional PII handling notes in the formal package.

Reviewer checklist (internal):
- [ ] Confirm sample event includes request_id, tenant_id, and trace_id
- [ ] Attach RBAC snapshot example for last 30 days
- [ ] Link to SIEM parser examples in repo
- [ ] Confirm KMS key export process documented

References and artifacts:
- Confluence: Evidence Portal Spec v1.4 (linked above)
- GitHub: audit-log-export repo (parser examples and CI tests)
- JIRA: SEC-452 (SIEM export adapter work)

Notes to self (tone: conversational, keep short):
- This is a condensed customer brief — don't overload with internal implementation detail.
- Keep onboarding timeline negotiable; customers often want 2-week sprints.
- Add a small FAQ at the bottom once we get common Qs from pilots.

Draft status: needs product review for wording on PII and signature options, and legal review for template NDA text required for S3 sharing.

Action items after review:
- Priya: add Splunk HEC ingestion example and minimal HEC config
- Diego: attach RBAC v2 snapshot export sample (anonymized)
- Avery: get legal to sign off on S3 + KMS data sharing clause

Last note: aim to turn this into a short Trust Center page: "Evidence ingestion options" + downloadable sample bundle, targeting customers starting SOC2 / vendor assurance reviews.
